oracle.description: Three oracles decide this together: test_release_scorecard_build.py (the new cost block), test_release_scorecard_worse.py (the detector reading the frontier half), and test_release_scorecard_kinds.py, whose only job is that the two kinds of number never get conflated again -- doubling the frontier figure must not move the billed total.

purpose: Stop build_scorecard from adding two numbers that are not the same kind. Its cost_usd block currently reports frontier, worker, and a total that is their sum -- but the frontier figure is computed by the Stop hook as tokens multiplied by a hardcoded 2025 list-price table, so nothing meters it and on a subscription plan it is never billed, while the worker figure is OpenCode's own step-finish accounting of real metered API spend that is actually charged. Adding an imputed list price to real money and calling it a total is a category error, and in the live run it read $241.43 of which eleven cents was money. A scorecard that reports that as a total will be read as spend by whoever opens it next, which is the exact failure the two-source design existed to prevent. Replace the block with exactly five keys. worker_billed_usd is the real metered spend that worker_totals reports, and is the only money in the system. frontier_usage_equivalent_usd is the imputed figure that frontier_totals reports, preserved and merely renamed -- the point is to label it, not to hide it. total_billed_usd equals worker_billed_usd, named so that a reader asking what this cost gets the true answer without having to know any of the above; there must be no key anywhere holding frontier plus worker, because that sum is the defect. commensurable is always False, stated in the data rather than only in a docstring so that a consumer can assert on it. total_reliable keeps its meaning, the worker half's cost_reported. Then make detect_worse's turns_flat_cost_up signal read frontier_usage_equivalent_usd rather than the old total: the frontier's own usage figure is what turns flat while cost rises is about, and it is the half that moves with coordinator behaviour, so a worker that costs more must not fire that alarm. Its values entries stay a turns and figure pair. Everything else is settled and must not change: reduce_sessions, frontier_totals, worker_spend_from_receipt, worker_totals, the loaders, the window filter, main and the entry point. Leave no debugging output behind.
required_outcomes: the cost block has exactly the five named keys and no sum of the two halves
total_billed_usd equals worker_billed_usd, even when the frontier figure is large
frontier_usage_equivalent_usd still carries frontier_totals' figure unchanged
commensurable is False for every input including empty ones
detect_worse reads the frontier usage figure, not a mixed total
a rising worker figure alone does not fire turns_flat_cost_up
nothing else in the module changes

acceptance_properties.requirement: an imputed figure is never added to real money
acceptance_properties.fails_when: doubling the sink rows' cost moves total_billed_usd, or any key holds frontier plus worker

acceptance_properties.requirement: the billed total is the billed total
acceptance_properties.fails_when: total_billed_usd differs from worker_billed_usd, the key set is not exactly the five names, or commensurable is not False

acceptance_properties.requirement: the worse-detector watches the frontier half
acceptance_properties.fails_when: turns_flat_cost_up reads a mixed total, or fires when only the worker figure rose

non_goals: the hook's pricing table, which is not this packet's to change
the loaders, the window filter, main and the entry point
hiding the frontier figure -- it is renamed and labelled, not removed
